entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Narendra Chaurasia - Govt. Advocate for respondent
Shri Jeetendra Kumar Dixit - Advocate for respondent No.2.
Appellant has filed I.A. No.22757/2023 an application under Section 389(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure for suspension of jail sentence.

2. Appellant has been convicted under Sections 450, 376 (1) and 506 of IPC and under Section 4 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 3 years, R.I. for 10 years, R.I. for 6 months and R.I. for 10 years respectively with total fine of Rs.12,000/-, with default stipulations.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant has challenged the judgment on grounds that Court below has committed an error in holding the age of victim to be below 18 years of age.
It is submitted that prosecution is unable to prove the said fact.
No declaration is given by parents in the admission register according to rules.
Principal has also not deposed that on what basis date of birth is mentioned in admission register.
It is further argued by counsel for appellant that mother herself says the age to be 17 years.
Age written in admission register is different and prosecutrix tells her age to be 16 yeas.
It is further submitted that there was long delay in sending the samples collected from prosecutrix for DNA examination.
Sample was collected from prosecutrix on 08.10.2020 and same was sent on 28.01.2021.
Prosecution failed to prove that sample was in safe custody and there was no chances of tampering with it.
Considering aforesaid circumstances, application for suspension of sentence be allowed.
4. Learned counsel appearing for objector opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
It is submitted that offence is serious in nature.
DNA report is positive and prosecutrix was minor.
PW-6 was examined before Court to establish that prosecutrix was below 18 years of age.
Government Advocate appearing for State also argues on same lines.
5. Heard the counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: Considering the fact that there was delay in sending the samples for examination and different date of birth has been mentioned by prosecution in evidence and on what basis date of birth has been recorded in register is also not clear.
It is also argued by counsel appearing for appellant that prosecutrix was consenting party.
7. Considering aforesaid circumstances of the case, I.A. No.22757/2023 for suspension of sentence is allowed.

8. It is hereby directed that the custodial sentence awarded to the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal and on deposit of fine, if already not paid, he shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 28.05.2024 and on other dates as may be fixed in this regard till final disposal of this appeal.
9. List the appeal for final hearing in due course.
10. C.C. as per rules.
(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE sp/-
